title: Constrained dissipation and the lifetime of quantum many-body scars
authors: Weyner Ccuiro, Rosario Fazio, Alessandro Silva
abstract: We investigate the fate of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model subject to Markovian dissipation. We show that when local jump operators respect the same symmetries of the Hamiltonian the full Liouvillian spectrum displays a tower of states with properties analogous to standard quantum scars: large overlaps with Néel states and equally spaced gaps in the imaginary part of the eigenvalues, set by a single frequency. Whether the long-time dynamics is dominated by scars is determined by the real parts of the eigenvalues, which are set by the ratio between the two relaxation rates $γ_{\pm}$ describing spin flips down-to-up or up-to-down respectively. For asymmetric dissipation ($γ_+ > γ_-$) the scarred eigenvalues have the smallest real parts: the resulting enhanced fidelity oscillations are further stabilized by staggered jump operators. In contrast, replacing the full projection operator in the dissipators with a partial one breaks the symmetries of the problem and is seen to destroy dissipative scars altogether.
summary: This paper analyzes the stability of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model under environmental dissipation. It shows that the preservation of scars requires the dissipation mechanism to respect the system's symmetries. Furthermore, the decay rate of quantum revivals is critically dependent on the asymmetry between gain and loss rates, demonstrating a clear mechanism for enhancing coherence through engineered dissipation.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum many-body scars (QMBS) survive and decay when the system is subjected to Markovian dissipation, particularly focusing on the role of symmetry in the dissipation process.
main_result: The persistence of scars requires local jump operators to respect the Hamiltonian symmetries; furthermore, asymmetric dissipation rates ($\gamma_+ > \gamma_-$) enhance the revival fidelity and stabilize the scar dynamics.
method: The analysis relies on diagonalizing the full Liouvillian spectrum and calculating the Uhlmann fidelity $F(t)$ using the biorthonormal basis expansion.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the PXP Hamiltonian, which simulates the nearest-neighbor blockade regime of Rydberg atom arrays. Dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating local jump operators.
key_observables: Fidelity $F(t)$, Liouvillian eigenvalues ($\lambda$), scar-dyad weights ($W_k$), and the evolution of local observables like staggered magnetization $\langle Z angle$.
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\gamma_+, \gamma_-$), the blockade parameter ($\alpha$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the first-order rate approximation for decay rates and critically depends on the strict kinetic constraint imposed by the Rydberg blockade.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overlap spectrum of eigenmodes with the Néel state, the decay of fidelity $F(t)$ under different dissipation schemes (staggered vs. uniform), and the evolution of local spin coherence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Liouvillian spectrum, first establishing the scar tower in the closed system, then introducing dissipation, and finally comparing the decay rates and revival dynamics under symmetric, asymmetric, and symmetry-breaking dissipation conditions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics in highly interacting platforms like Rydberg arrays, providing quantitative rules for how dissipation affects fragile quantum coherence features like scars.
